title: NewsArticle
description: A published article or report from a named outlet. THREE DIFFERENT PROVIDERS FEED IT with three different key models and no shared id: the RSS feed ships six always-present string keys with NO id at all (an absent feed element is the empty string, never null - a deliberate contract so a consumer never has to branch on key presence); khala's reports are identified by a report SLUG and only the 'latest' variant carries dates, resolved by fetching each report page; CryptoRank's news rows carry a provider numeric id. published_at is therefore nullable and PROVIDER-FORMATTED in two of the three cases - it is never our clock. There is NO canonical article identity in the repo (canonical-model.md section 2).

article_id.description: Null today: no provider mints a usable id and there is no canonical one. Present so a dedup key can be added without a shape change.

url.description: The article link. In khala's case the report URL is stable and the slug is derived from it - for the news family this is the de-facto identity.

summary.description: Null when the feed element is absent (khala) or clipped to 200 runes (news strips HTML).

published_at.description: Provider time when reported. Null means NOT REPORTED - the UI must render an em-dash and never a date, and never 0. This is a real case, not an edge case: khala's homepage list source publishes no dates at all.

published_raw.description: The provider's own date text, unparsed (an RSS pubDate string or khala's 'Mon D, YYYY' byline). Kept because two of three providers give no instant, and guessing one from a locale-formatted string is exactly the fabrication the repo forbids.

related_coins.description: Provider-matched coin snapshots attached to the article. Matching happened UPSTREAM - there is no coin-to-article matcher in this repo, and a consumer must not read this list as our own association.

related_coin.description: A related-coin snapshot with its own nullable price - absence stays absent.
